In this way, the manufacturer could increase the average fuel economy of its nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR. A rating change of this nature can be accomplished easily by a manufacturer, either by making relatively small modifications to the nonpassenger automobiles (i.e., adding heavier springs), or in some cases, where the vehicles have excess capacity, by merely making a paper change to their rating. Such a shift would have the same type of effect on average fuel economy as the shift from buying nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR to buying nonpassenger automobiles above 6,000 pounds GVWR.
